text.en: A mature human red blood cell has no nucleus.
Every living cell has a well-defined nucleus.

modelCorrection.en: Bacteria have no well-defined nucleus, and mature human red blood cells have no nucleus.

text.en: Bacteria have no DNA, because they have no well-defined nucleus.

modelCorrection.en: Bacteria have one circular DNA molecule in a region called the nucleoid.

text.en: Chromosomes are visible as rods only when a cell is about to divide.

explanation.en: A nucleus is not found in every cell, and DNA is not found only in a nucleus.
